answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a canyon as the anchor of the cost.
